goal.en: Control how likely, how necessary and how habitual you make something sound.
goal.ar: أن تتحكم في درجة الاحتمال والضرورة والاعتياد التي توحي بها جملتك.

head: Expression
Roughly
Example
rows: The talks are likely to continue.
There is no chance of that.

text.en: “May”, “might” and “could” are close in meaning here. “May not” means possibly not; “cannot” means impossible — a much stronger claim.
text.ar: الأفعال may وmight وcould متقاربة في هذا المعنى. لكن may not تعني «ربما لا»، أما cannot فتعني الاستحالة، وهي أقوى بكثير.

text.en: In writing, an unhedged prediction is a claim you must defend. “Prices will rise” invites disagreement; “prices are likely to rise” does not.
text.ar: التنبؤ بلا تحفّظ ادعاء عليك الدفاع عنه. فجملة Prices will rise تستدعي الاعتراض، بخلاف are likely to rise.

head: Form
Meaning
rows: It was necessary, and I paid.
It was not necessary (so probably I didn't).
I paid, but it turned out to be unnecessary.
I didn't pay, and that was wrong.

text.en: “Needn't have + participle” always means the action HAPPENED and was wasted. “Didn't need to” usually means it never happened.
text.ar: تركيب needn't have مع التصريف الثالث يعني أن الفعل وقع فعلاً وكان بلا داعٍ، أما didn't need to فتعني غالباً أنه لم يقع أصلاً.

items.en: We needn't have hurried — the train was late anyway.
items.ar: لم يكن علينا أن نستعجل، فقد تأخر القطار على أي حال.

items.en: I didn't need to bring my passport, so I left it at home.
items.ar: لم أكن مضطراً لإحضار جواز سفري، فتركته في البيت.

text.en: used to + base verb covers past habits AND past states: “I used to live in Aswan.” “Would” covers repeated actions only — never states.
text.ar: used to مع الفعل المجرد تصلح للعادات والحالات الماضية معاً. أما would فتصلح للأفعال المتكررة فقط لا للحالات.

head: Correct
Wrong
rows: I used to have a bike.
I'm used to the noise now.
I used to the noise now.

text.en: “Used to do” (past habit) and “be used to doing” (accustomed) are different structures. “I am used to waking up early” means it feels normal now.
text.ar: تركيب used to do للعادة الماضية، وتركيب be used to doing للاعتياد الحالي. فجملة I am used to waking up early تعني أن الأمر صار مألوفاً لي الآن.

questions.sentence: With this demand, prices ___ to rise before the summer.
options: are likely
are liking
are like
likely are

explanation.en: “Be likely to + verb” is the standard hedged prediction.
explanation.ar: تركيب be likely to هو صيغة التنبؤ المتحفّظ المعتادة.

prompt.en: Which sentence claims the strongest certainty?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تدّعي أعلى درجة يقين؟

options: The deal is bound to go ahead.
The deal is likely to go ahead.
The deal could well go ahead.
The deal may possibly go ahead.

explanation.en: “Bound to” is near-certainty; the rest are graded possibilities.
explanation.ar: bound to تقارب اليقين، أما البقية فدرجات من الاحتمال.

prompt.en: What is the difference between “He may not come” and “He cannot come”?
prompt.ar: ما الفرق بين He may not come وHe cannot come؟

options: The first is possible absence; the second is impossibility.
The first is impossibility; the second is possible absence.
They mean exactly the same thing in every context.
The first refers to the past; the second to the future.

explanation.en: “May not” hedges; “cannot” rules the option out entirely.
explanation.ar: may not تتحفّظ، أما cannot فتستبعد الاحتمال تماماً.

prompt.en: Which sentence is safest in a report where the evidence is thin?
prompt.ar: أي جملة أسلم في تقرير أدلته ضعيفة؟

options: The change may partly explain the fall in sales.
The change is the reason for the fall in sales.
The change definitely caused the fall in sales.
Everyone knows the change caused the fall.

explanation.en: “May partly explain” matches a weak evidence base; the others overclaim.
explanation.ar: عبارة may partly explain تناسب ضعف الدليل، أما البقية فمبالغة في الجزم.

prompt.en: “We needn't have booked a table.” What happened?
prompt.ar: «We needn't have booked a table» ماذا حدث؟

options: We booked one, and it turned out to be unnecessary.
We did not book, and that caused a problem.
We were not allowed to book a table at all.
We will book a table if it becomes necessary.

explanation.en: “Needn't have + participle” always means the action happened and was wasted.
explanation.ar: needn't have مع التصريف الثالث تعني دائماً أن الفعل وقع وكان بلا داعٍ.

questions.sentence: I ___ take my passport, so I left it in the hotel safe.
options: didn't need to
needn't have
mustn't have
shouldn't have

explanation.en: It was not necessary and it did not happen → didn't need to.
explanation.ar: لم يكن ضرورياً ولم يحدث، فنستخدم didn't need to.

prompt.en: Match the form with what actually happened.

pairs: I paid, but it was wasted
I didn't pay, and I regret it

explanation.en: These four look similar and mean four different things — this is a classic B2 trap.
explanation.ar: هذه الصيغ الأربع متشابهة الشكل مختلفة المعنى تماماً، وهي فخّ معروف في هذا المستوى.

options: We mustn't have worried so much about it.
We needn't have worried so much about it.
We shouldn't have worried so much then.
We didn't have to worry about it at all.

explanation.en: “Mustn't have” is not used for past necessity; “needn't have” is the form.
explanation.ar: لا تُستعمل mustn't have للضرورة في الماضي، والصيغة الصحيحة needn't have.

questions.sentence: We ___ spend every summer at my grandmother's house.
options: used to
use to
are used to
would have

explanation.en: A repeated past habit → used to + base verb.
explanation.ar: عادة ماضية متكررة، فنستخدم used to مع الفعل المجرد.

options: I would have a motorbike when I was young.
I used to have a motorbike when I was young.
I would ride my motorbike every weekend.
I often rode my motorbike to the coast.

explanation.en: “Would” works for repeated actions, not for states. Owning something is a state → used to have.
explanation.ar: would تصلح للأفعال المتكررة لا للحالات. والملكية حالة، فنقول used to have.

prompt.en: “I'm used to working nights.” What does this mean?
prompt.ar: ماذا تعني I'm used to working nights؟

options: Night work feels normal to me now.
I worked nights in the past but stopped.
I have to start working nights soon.
I have never worked at night before.

explanation.en: “Be used to + -ing” means accustomed. “Used to work nights” would mean a past habit.
explanation.ar: be used to مع ing تعني الاعتياد الحالي، أما used to work فتعني عادة ماضية انتهت.

options: Did you use to live in Alexandria?
Did you used to live in Alexandria?
Do you used to live in Alexandria?
Were you use to live in Alexandria?

explanation.en: After “did”, the verb returns to its base form: use to.
explanation.ar: بعد did يعود الفعل مجرداً: use to.

questions.answer: The results are unlikely to change the policy

explanation.ar: فعل الكون ثم unlikely ثم to مع الفعل المجرد.

prompt.en: Rewrite with “used to”: “I played football every Friday, but I stopped years ago.” → “I ___ football every Friday.”
prompt.ar: أعد الصياغة باستخدام used to: I ___ football every Friday.

explanation.en: “Used to” marks a habit that has now ended — the “but not any more” is built in.
explanation.ar: used to تدل على عادة انتهت، ومعنى «لم يعد» مضمَّن فيها.

prompt.en: A colleague asks whether the project will finish on time. Which reply is most professional?
prompt.ar: سألك زميل إن كان المشروع سينتهي في موعده. أي رد أكثر مهنية؟

options: It's possible, though the testing phase could still delay us.
Yes, definitely, there is absolutely no risk at all here.
I have no idea about that, ask somebody else instead.
Maybe yes, maybe no, it is really hard to say anything.

explanation.en: It commits to a position and names the risk. Overclaiming and shrugging are both weaker.
explanation.ar: الرد الأول يلتزم بموقف ويسمّي المخاطرة، أما المبالغة والتهرب فكلاهما أضعف.
